## Building the Bridge {#matrix background-color="#FFFFFF"}

::: {.lede}
Meeting users where they’re at.
:::

::: {.fill .fill--center}
```{=html}

  <thead>
    <tr><th>Layer</th><th>Who</th><th>What it&rsquo;s for</th><th>What it takes</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>

      <td>The output, <br>no code at all</td>
```

:::

::: {.notes}
**Jadey:** All of this comes back to knowing who you're building for. Every layer we built made the same reports available to someone who couldn't access it before. With each layer out, we lowered a barrier and made it easier for more people to get to the insights. First, it was just editing the main Quarto template, then installing the {soils} package and running a script, then finally, just clicking a button. Same analysis the whole way through. The only thing that changed was who could get to it.

**Tanya:** Most of us are at the first layer. We built something to make our own work easier, and that's the right layer for a lot of people. Some of us are at the second, because others on our team want to use it and adapt it. And some of us are at the third, because the people who need the answer are never going to open an IDE.

Each layer is the right layer for someone. What determines which one you need isn't the tool, and it isn't what you already know how to build. It's one question, before you build: who is this for?

**[click: quote]**
:::

. . .

```{=html}
<p class="quote" style="margin-top:40px;background:#2c5e3b"><span class="mark" style="color:#d8dfd7">&ldquo;</span>The right tool is the one that gets the insight into the right hands.</p>
```

::: {.notes}
**Jadey:** Build the layer that gets the insight into their hands. Then let it show you where the other layers need to grow.
:::
